flashcards.q: Give the two mechanisms that make random k-fold CV invalid on financial data.
flashcards.a: (1) Serial dependence: near-duplicates of test observations sit in training. (2) Forward-looking labels: a train sample at t carries info about events in [t, t+H); if that window crosses the test boundary the train set contains test answers. Measured: corr(train-tail labels, test-head labels) ~ +0.66 under naive adjacency.

flashcards.q: State the purge rule and how to size the gap.
flashcards.a: Delete any training sample whose label window [t, t+H) intersects the test block; gap >= MAXIMUM label horizon (max holding of triple-barrier), never the average exit. Use event time aligned to label metadata, not hardcoded calendar days.

flashcards.q: What is embargo and why is it needed on top of purging?
flashcards.a: Strip a buffer AFTER each test block before that region re-enters LATER folds' training sets. Purge handles label overlap before test; embargo blocks feature-side serial dependence (persistent signals, vol state) from carrying test info backward into subsequent fits. Default ~1% of bars, sized by measured feature ACF half-lives.

flashcards.q: Is fitting StandardScaler on full data harmful? Which models care and which don't?
flashcards.a: Plain unregularized OLS: prediction-invariant to affine scaling (slope absorbs constants) - harmless there but still bad practice. Harmful for ridge/LASSO (penalty geometry), kNN/SVM (distances), neural nets (optimization dynamics). Rule: fit inside folds unconditionally - exceptions breed complacency.

flashcards.q: What does Combinatorially Purged CV add over single-path walk-forward?
flashcards.a: Evaluates all C(N,k) combinations of test sub-blocks with purge/embargo per combination, so every observation tests multiple times in different contexts - output is a DISTRIBUTION of performance paths ('90% of paths exceed 0.8 Sharpe') instead of one noisy draw. Costs combinatorial compute; measures robustness, does not fix overfitting by itself.

flashcards.q: Define Probability of Backtest Overfitting and interpret PBO=0.45.
flashcards.a: Via CSCV: pick the best configuration in-sample per combination, check its out-of-sample rank; PBO = fraction of combinations where IS-best lands below OOS median. 0.45 = coin flip: selection process found noise. Below ~0.2 credible; above 0.5 actively anti-selects. PBO audits your CHOICE process, not whether alpha exists.

flashcards.q: List the inputs of the Deflated Sharpe Ratio and what each corrects.
flashcards.a: Number of trials N (expected max-SR under null rises with search), variance of trial Sharpes (dispersion raises expected max), sample length (SR estimation error), skewness and excess kurtosis (fat tails inflate SR error). Output: probability true SR>0 given you observed best-of-N. Undercounting N launders snooping.

flashcards.q: Positions held H days: why do iid daily-PnL t-stats lie, by roughly how much, and fixes?
flashcards.a: Daily PnL from overlapping positions is MA(H-1)-dependent; iid SE understates truth ~sqrt(H) (measured 3.33x at H=10 vs theory 3.16). A lucky t=2 becomes ~0.6 honest. Fixes: Newey-West/HAC with lag>=H, trade-level (per-position) PnL aggregation, or moving-block/stationary bootstrap (Politis-Romano).

flashcards.q: Name three ways raw data leaks future information even with perfect splits.
flashcards.a: (1) Survivorship: today's constituents/delisted-absent universes remove left tails. (2) Restatement lookahead: fundamentals joined on period instead of announcement date. (3) Timestamp fiction: executing on bar-close signals AT that close, retroactive split adjustments shown to historical models. All need point-in-time/bitemporal infrastructure.

flashcards.q: What thresholds/corrections exist for trying many strategies on one dataset?
flashcards.a: Harvey-Liu-Zhu: t>3.0 for new factor claims (316 published factors -> false discovery control). Harvey-Liu Backtesting: ~50% haircut on reported Sharpe for typical searches. Bailey-Lopez de Prado DSR: analytic probability adjustment given N trials + return moments. White Reality Check / Hansen SPA: econometric gold standard over defined candidate sets. Keep a trial registry - N drives everything.

flashcards.q: Order the gates of a complete meta-labeling strategy validation.
flashcards.a: 1 PIT/bitemporal data, delisting-complete universe. 2 Triple-barrier labels matched to holding intent. 3 Features lagged >= decision latency; preprocessing fit inside folds. 4 Anchored walk-forward with purge=horizon, embargo=max(1% bars, ACF memory). 5 Hyperparams on inner slices only. 6 HAC/bootstrap CIs + CPCV paths + DSR/PBO over registered N. 7 Cost model stress (spread+impact+borrow). 8 Paper-trade shadow >= several embargo lengths reconciled live-vs-backtest.

flashcards.q: Why does even statistically immaculate validation overstate achievable PnL?
flashcards.a: Statistics fix information flow, not execution physics: adverse selection on crossing fills, square-root-law impact (~sigma*sqrt(Q/V)), spread paid for immediacy, latency drift between signal and arrival, partial fills, capacity decay. Realistic costs commonly eat 30-80% of gross backtest Sharpe - calibrate from your own TCA data, not flat bps.

flashcards.q: PM says 'TimeSeriesSplit makes us leak-free.' What's the precise correction?
flashcards.a: sklearn TimeSeriesSplit respects temporal order but implements NO purging or embargo: boundaries leak exactly where labels have horizons (+0.66-correlation demo), and expanding trains re-ingest prior test windows unprotected. Wrap a ~20-line purged/embargoed splitter, print fold gaps as evidence, add fold-fitted preprocessing + trial registry.

flashcards.q: Purged folds kept 78% of naive train size in the lab demo. How do you justify losing data?
flashcards.a: 78% honest beats 100% contaminated: leaked backtests flatter until capital compounds the fiction. Budget the gap explicitly (longer history, lower decision frequency, event-time alignment), report both naive and purged numbers during research so the delta itself quantifies how much self-deception was on offer.
